newsitem.title: CONGO: Zaire peace talks cancelled -- U.N. official.
newsitem.headline: Zaire peace talks cancelled -- U.N. official.

text.p: Peace talks scheduled between President Mobutu Sese Seko of Zaire and rebel leader Laurent Kabila were cancelled on Wednesday when Kabila refused to board a South African ship in the Congolese port of Pointe Noire, U.N. envoy Mohamed Sahnoun said.

Sahnoun told reporters aboard the ship Kabila insisted at the last minute that the talks should take place in international waters, a demand rejected by South African President Nelson Mandela, who was to have chaired the meeting.
The second face-to-face meeting between Mobutu and Kabila was to have taken place at 11 a.m. (1000 GMT) but was repeatedly postponed amidst confusion about Kabila's whereabouts.
Sahnoun said Kabila told Mandela by telephone he was concerned about his security and would join the ship only if it sailed into international waters.
"President Mandela said the ship will not go to the high sea for the meeting and therefore the meeting will not be held," Sahnoun said.
He did not say what the next step would be in the South African-led bid to avert a bloody showdown between followers of Mobutu and Kabila in the streets of Kinshasa.
